sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
1. Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning.
2. Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps.
3. Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with decompression illness.
Patient Selection Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 2 or higher.
2. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
3. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
4. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
1. Treatment for chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency alone is not covered.
2. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema.
3. Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in hyperbaric oxygen therapy. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in undersea and hyperbaric medicine.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 30 treatments within a 30-day period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. When hyperbaric oxygen therapy continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
2. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment.
3. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for hyperbaric oxygen therapy:
1. E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
3. T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment was furnished. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected. Report the date of the initial treatment on the claim.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: Fictional Society of Undersea and Hyperbaric Medicine. Clinical practice guideline for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. 2019 edition.

sections.heading: Contractor Contact Information
sections.text: Inquiries may be submitted to the fictional contractor medical review department at (555) 0177-5860.
